Definition: roomy, in any (or every) direction, literally or figuratively
BiblicalUsage: Rachab means roomy, broad, spacious — in any direction, literal or figurative. God promised to bring Israel 'unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey'; Hamor said of Jacob's family, 'the land, behold, it is large enough for them'; and Isaiah says the LORD will be 'unto us a place of broad rivers and streams.'
TheologicalSignificance: The point for me is that God's largeness is not waste but welcome: He gives a large land, a large heart, and room enough for His people.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
